summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of fibrosing mesenteritis, chronic GI dysmotility, and hepatitis C, was admitted for abdominal pain, vomiting, and dehydration. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction but revealed fecal loading in the colon. She was managed with IV fluids, electrolyte replacement, G-tube drainage, and IV pain control, transitioning to oral medications as symptoms improved. Her potassium was corrected, and her subtherapeutic INR was addressed with Lovenox bridging until therapeutic on warfarin. Liver ultrasound showed fatty infiltration, likely related to chronic hepatitis C, with plans for outpatient follow-up. She tolerated a soft diet, had stable vital signs, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.
